facts.text: The contract clause 27 is headed “Final Certificate”.
Clause 27 comes after clause 26, which is headed “Practical Completion”.
Clause 27.1 states that, unless stated elsewhere in the contract, the builder is not required to obtain any certificate of occupancy or final inspection certificate relating to the building works.
Clause 29 is headed “Defects Liability Period”.
Clause 29.1 states that the defects liability period is 26 weeks commencing on and including the date of practical completion.
In clause 29.1, the standard form 13-week period was struck through and “26” was inserted and initialled.
Clause 29.2 states that the owner may, before the end of the defects liability period, give the builder a list of defects that appear after the date of practical completion.
Clause 29.3 states that the builder must rectify defects that are the builder’s responsibility and which are notified to the builder during the defects liability period.
Clause 14 of Schedule 1 specifies that Tender No 2277 dated 22 January 2009 forms part of the contract.
The Tender specifies that the basic tender price includes the Council Development Application and Inspection Fees.
The Tender specifies that the tender price does not include provision of the FOC.

The Tender specifies work to be completed by the owners prior to the issue of an occupation certificate, including items 18, 19, and 20 concerning lighting and the installation of outdoor and indoor clothes lines.
The user states that the Tribunal misinterpreted the contract when it concluded that the builder was responsible for obtaining the FOC as part of the works to be carried out.
The user states that the contract (including the Tender) does not otherwise provide that the builder is responsible for obtaining the FOC.
The user states that a FOC is not a building or planning approval.
The user quotes Moore J in Toplace Pty Ltd v The Council of the City of Sydney [2020] NSWLEC 121 at [16] about when a Final Occupation Certificate can be issued.
The user states that an FOC certifies that the completed building (or part of the building) is suitable for occupation or use.
The user states that an FOC is a certification of completed building works, not a part of the building works.
The user states that clause 27 refers to a certificate “relating to the building works”.
The user states that a certificate relating to building works cannot be part of the building works.
The user states that the definition of building works in clause 1 refers to building works to be carried out, completed and handed over to the owner.
The user states that, in this contract, the owners were required to undertake works prior to an occupation certificate being issued.
The user states that the building works “handed over” to the owner could not include the provision of the FOC.
